parsed.explanation: Section 4 defines v(B) as the nested difference of the decreasing order b_1>=...>=b_r, and the strategy explicitly processes b_2,...,b_r in that order, concluding D(M)=v(B)<=T_n by citing Theorem 4.2. But Theorem 4.2's proof, via Lemma 4.1, only produces some (greedy) ordering of P∪N with nested difference g<=S/(2^m-1); it never shows the decreasing ordering attains this, and the strategy never uses the constructed ordering. So the theorem's stated conclusion (decreasing-order chain value small) does not follow from what is proved, and the upper bound, as written, rests on an unproven statement; no repair appears elsewhere. (The stated theorem is in fact true—one can show by adjacent swaps that sorting decreasing never increases a nested difference—but that argument is not in the text.) The one-line fix (process the greedy ordering) is exactly what the objection demands.
